documents.title: OWASP Top 10 A01: Broken Access Control
documents.content_origin: Sentinel-authored reviewed summary; no upstream prose is reproduced.
documents.content: Broken access control occurs when a server does not enforce the authorization decision for the requested object or action. Check that object identifiers and administrative routes are authorized on the server for every request.

documents.title: OWASP Top 10 A02: Cryptographic Failures
documents.content_origin: Sentinel-authored reviewed summary; no upstream prose is reproduced.
documents.content: Cryptographic failures expose sensitive data when protection in transit, at rest, or in key handling is absent or misused. Verify transport protection and avoid logging credentials or secrets.

documents.title: OWASP Top 10 A03: Injection
documents.content_origin: Sentinel-authored reviewed summary; no upstream prose is reproduced.
documents.content: Injection includes SQL Injection and Cross-Site Scripting when untrusted input is interpreted as part of a command, query, or page. Keep data separate from code through parameter binding and context-appropriate output encoding.

documents.title: OWASP Top 10 A04: Insecure Design
documents.content_origin: Sentinel-authored reviewed summary; no upstream prose is reproduced.
documents.content: Insecure design is a missing or ineffective control in the intended system design. Record abuse cases and require a server-side control before assuming client validation is sufficient.

documents.title: OWASP Top 10 A05: Security Misconfiguration
documents.content_origin: Sentinel-authored reviewed summary; no upstream prose is reproduced.
documents.content: Security misconfiguration includes unsafe defaults, unnecessary features, verbose errors, and missing hardening. Review deployed configuration rather than relying only on source-code intent.

documents.title: OWASP Top 10 A06: Vulnerable and Outdated Components
documents.content_origin: Sentinel-authored reviewed summary; no upstream prose is reproduced.
documents.content: Vulnerable and outdated components are dependencies with known or unsupported security exposure. Inventory versions and review scanner evidence before assigning affected application scope.

documents.title: OWASP Top 10 A07: Identification and Authentication Failures
documents.content_origin: Sentinel-authored reviewed summary; no upstream prose is reproduced.
documents.content: Authentication failures occur when identity proofing, credentials, session management, or recovery controls are weak. Treat authentication evidence separately from authorization evidence.

documents.title: OWASP Top 10 A08: Software and Data Integrity Failures
documents.content_origin: Sentinel-authored reviewed summary; no upstream prose is reproduced.
documents.content: Software and data integrity failures arise when updates, serialized data, or build inputs are trusted without verification. Pin and verify trusted artifacts before use.

documents.title: OWASP Top 10 A09: Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
documents.content_origin: Sentinel-authored reviewed summary; no upstream prose is reproduced.
documents.content: Logging and monitoring failures prevent detection or investigation of security-relevant events. Preserve useful evidence while redacting sensitive values before durable logs or model input.

documents.title: OWASP Top 10 A10: Server-Side Request Forgery
documents.content_origin: Sentinel-authored reviewed summary; no upstream prose is reproduced.
documents.content: Server-Side Request Forgery occurs when a server fetches an attacker-controlled destination. Validate and allowlist destinations at the final network boundary and reject redirects outside the authorized origin.

documents.title: Nuclei documentation
documents.content_origin: Sentinel-authored reviewed summary; no upstream prose is reproduced.
documents.content: Nuclei runs template-defined checks. A charter scan must use a reviewed, committed template allowlist and retain only sanitized result evidence.

documents.title: Trivy documentation
documents.content_origin: Sentinel-authored reviewed summary; no upstream prose is reproduced.
documents.content: Trivy identifies configuration and dependency issues from supplied artifacts. Treat a scanner result as evidence that needs location, rule, and severity context rather than proof of exploitability.

documents.title: Semgrep documentation
documents.content_origin: Sentinel-authored reviewed summary; no upstream prose is reproduced.
documents.content: Semgrep is a static analysis engine that matches code against rules. Treat its rule ID, severity, path, and line range as sanitized evidence; do not persist scanner message, source-line, or fix text.
